mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above the prior quarter's growth rate signals improving demand conditions, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > prior quarter for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above the prior quarter's growth rate signals improving supply conditions, which reduces inflation pressure and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > prior quarter for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month period where the federal funds rate exceeds 5.5% signals a restrictive monetary stance, which increases discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) below the prior quarter's growth rate signals weakening demand conditions, which reduces earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < prior quarter for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals an overheating labor market, which increases inflation pressure and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
